description: Six fictional company documents and prepared excerpts from two real manuals. Not operational factory guidance.

sections.heading: External repair visits
sections.text:
# External repair visits

This is an original, fictional company procedure for the Soverius Chocolate RAG lab. All roles, contact routes, and approval rules below are invented for the exercise. It is not an operational safety procedure for a real factory.

sections.heading: 1. Start with the incident
sections.text:
## 1. Start with the incident

When an incident appears to require outside repair expertise, the shift manager asks the maintenance coordinator to assess the need for a visit. The request must identify the incident, affected room and equipment, observed symptoms, and any checks already completed.

The maintenance coordinator selects an appropriate service provider and agrees the proposed work. An equipment manual may help identify the relevant expertise, but it does not authorize a visit, room access, or repair.

The cooling-room incident procedure remains responsible for temperature-related escalation. This document adds the external-visit process; it does not change temperature limits or incident-resolution conditions.

sections.heading: 2. Contact the responsible role
sections.text:
## 2. Contact the responsible role

The lab uses role-based contact routes rather than personal telephone numbers. These routes are fictional records, not connected communication tools.

| Need | First contact | Fictional contact route | If unavailable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Report the incident and coordinate the current shift | Shift manager | Operations duty desk | Plant duty manager |
| Arrange a repair provider and define the work | Maintenance coordinator | Maintenance duty queue | Plant duty manager assigns a qualified maintenance delegate |
| Arrange arrival, check-in, and a temporary badge | Reception/security | Visitor desk | Plant duty manager arranges an authorized check-in officer |
| Decide how products and production areas must be protected | Quality representative | Quality duty queue | Plant duty manager contacts the quality backup |
| Resolve a missing owner or staffing problem | Plant duty manager | Plant duty desk | Visit remains pending until an authorized owner is available |

The current duty roster supplies the person assigned to each role and their current contact details. If that roster is not available, report the missing information. Do not invent a name, phone number, or claim that someone has been contacted.

The plant duty manager may coordinate backups but cannot replace a required maintenance or quality approval merely by being the most senior person present.

sections.heading: 3. Create a repair-visit record
4. Check in and enter the agreed room
sections.text:
## 4. Check in and enter the agreed room

Technicians report to the visitor desk and quote the repair-visit reference. Reception/security verifies their identity against the expected visitor record, confirms the host is available, and records arrival. An unexpected substitute must be confirmed by the maintenance coordinator before access is issued.

The host provides the site briefing, including the agreed route, emergency arrangements, local hygiene requirements, and permitted areas. Any required protective clothing and hygiene steps must be completed before entering a production room.

The temporary badge identifies the approved visit and access period. It does not authorize independent movement around the factory. External technicians remain escorted by the host or an explicitly assigned replacement. If the escort leaves without a handover, technicians return to the designated waiting area.

Room-specific rules for this fictional site:

- **Cooling room:** arrange access without propping open the connecting door. Keep tools and parts away from stored batches and preserve access to walkways. Door position is confirmed by a person; the application has no door sensor.
- **Packaging hall:** use the agreed access route. Keep repair materials away from exposed product and packaging. Entry for observation does not authorize work on the packaging line.

Access to one room does not imply access to the other. A changed work location requires an updated visit record and approval for that area.

sections.heading: 5. Obtain permission to start the repair
sections.text:
## 5. Obtain permission to start the repair

Arrival, briefing, and room access allow the technician to reach the agreed location. They do not authorize repair work to begin.

At the equipment, the technician and maintenance approver confirm the scope and the required controls. Where applicable, authorized site personnel establish and verify equipment isolation under the site's separate isolation procedure. The technician must not infer that equipment is isolated because it appears idle or because the monitoring dashboard shows no activity.

The maintenance approver records permission to start. For work in the Cooling room or Packaging hall, the quality representative must also record that the agreed product and area protections are ready. Any separately required work permit must be in place.

If the required procedure, permit, or approval is missing, the visit stays at **waiting for work authorization**. The assistant should identify the missing item and responsible role.

If diagnosis reveals work outside the agreed scope, pause the affected work and ask the maintenance coordinator to update the plan. Permission to inspect a cooling unit does not automatically authorize electrical modifications or work on nearby equipment.

sections.heading: 6. Hand back the area and close the visit
sections.text:
## 6. Hand back the area and close the visit

The technician records the work performed, parts replaced, remaining issues, and any restrictions. The host checks that tools, spare parts, waste, and temporary barriers have been accounted for and the area has been left ready for review.

Maintenance confirms technical readiness. Quality confirms the production area's readiness and any product restrictions. The shift manager authorizes operational restart only after the necessary maintenance and quality releases are recorded.

Reception/security records departure and closes the temporary access. A technician leaving the site does not mean the equipment is ready to restart. Similarly, closing a repair visit does not resolve the original incident: recovery must still be established under the applicable incident procedure.

sections.heading: 7. What counts as evidence
sections.text:
## 7. What counts as evidence

| Visit state | Required record |
| --- | --- |
| Requested | Incident link and request for external support |
| Scheduled | Agreed scope, expected technicians, host, and appointment |
| Checked in | Verified arrival and visitor registration |
| Ready for room entry | Completed briefing, area requirements, and escort assignment |
| Authorized to work | Required maintenance and quality approvals, plus applicable controls and permits |
| Handed back | Repair report and the recorded readiness decisions |
| Visit closed | Departure and closure of temporary access |

These records are distinct. A statement such as “I will call maintenance” records an intention, not completed contact. An assistant-generated checklist is guidance, not proof that its steps have been performed. In the lab, human confirmations are explicitly marked as simulated.

sections.heading: 8. Information that must come from other records
sections.text:
## 8. Information that must come from other records

This procedure does not contain current duty assignments, actual contact details, an approved contractor list, room access maps, detailed hygiene instructions, equipment-isolation instructions, or completed visit approvals. Retrieve the relevant current record when available. If it has not been supplied to the lab, identify it as missing rather than filling the gap with an assumption.

sections.heading: Cooling-room incident response
sections.text:
# Cooling-room incident response

Original fictional training procedure. The limits below exist only for this software exercise. They do not establish safe chocolate storage, product release, or refrigeration settings.

sections.heading: Incident CR-2026-0920
sections.text:
## Incident CR-2026-0920

The training clock is fixed at 20 September 2026, 14:30 UTC. The Cooling room normally shows a warning during the noon-to-14:00 transfer period. In this scenario its temperature remains elevated after 14:00. Compare today's measurements with the previous day's same time window. Report the measurement period and UTC time explicitly.

The sample cooling-room temperature warning starts above 18 °C. This is an invented dashboard threshold. It does not establish that any batch is safe or unsafe. The quality representative owns product decisions.

sections.heading: Initial assessment
sections.text:
## Initial assessment

The operator checks the observation time, affected room and metric. Review temperature, humidity, supply-air temperature and cooling-unit power together. A temperature reading describes a condition, not its cause. Check whether the data has gaps before summarising a trend.

Ask the shift manager to coordinate a person at the room. The application has no door-position sensor. A person must inspect the connecting door and record the observation. Do not infer an open door from temperature alone. Do not report that an inspection happened unless a record confirms it.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text:
## Escalation

If the warning continues beyond the expected transfer period, the shift manager requests a maintenance assessment. The current duty roster identifies the on-duty role holders and contact routes. Missing contact information must be reported explicitly.

The maintenance coordinator decides whether external support is needed. Follow SOV-FAC-EXT-01 for arranging a visit. Equipment manuals supply possible checks but do not grant site access or permission to repair.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.text:
## Recovery

The shift manager records the operational decision after maintenance and quality supply the required releases. Resolving a monitoring incident requires evidence of recovery and the applicable human decision. The assistant may summarise evidence and propose next checks. It cannot release products, restart equipment or close this incident.

sections.heading: Technician brief for visit V-042
sections.text:
# Technician brief for visit V-042

Original fictional training record. The external technician account represents the visitor assigned to V-042. Every record here is simulated.

sections.heading: Assignment
sections.text:
## Assignment

Visit V-042 concerns assessment of the cooling unit in the Cooling room for incident CR-2026-0920. The fictional provider is Example Refrigeration. The internal host is Sam Example. The appointment is 20 September 2026 at 15:00 UTC. The record is currently scheduled. It does not contain arrival, briefing, maintenance approval or quality approval.

sections.heading: Arrival and access
sections.text:
## Arrival and access

Report to the Visitor desk and quote V-042. The fictional contact route is visitors@example.invalid. Wait for the host and the recorded check-in. Follow the host's approved route to the Cooling room and remain escorted. This visit provides no access to the Packaging hall.

sections.heading: Work status
sections.text:
## Work status

The scheduled appointment does not authorize repair work. The maintenance approver and quality representative must record their required approvals before work starts. Missing approvals keep the work pending. A chatbot response cannot supply those approvals.

sections.heading: Missing information
sections.text:
## Missing information

This brief contains no live phone numbers, completed inspection results, equipment-isolation instructions or approved work permits. Request the missing record from the responsible host. Do not invent it.

sections.heading: Cooling equipment training register
sections.text: # Cooling equipment training register

sections.heading: Lab equipment mapping
sections.text:
## Lab equipment mapping

For this exercise, equipment COOL-01 in the Cooling room references the Danfoss Optyma Cooler manual AN378367211987en-US0101 and the Danfoss AK-RC 305W-SD controller guide BC419723137674en-000202. This is a fictional teaching association, not evidence of an installed, approved or compatible real-world assembly.

sections.heading: Evidence boundaries
sections.text:
## Evidence boundaries

Manufacturer manuals describe product functions and possible fault causes. They do not establish the factory's actual configuration, current measurements or completed maintenance. Cite the relevant manual and PDF page. Distinguish PDF page numbers from numbers printed inside the document.

No installed parameter export or wiring diagram for a real site is available. Do not recommend a new setpoint or electrical change based on an assumed installation. Route equipment-specific decisions to the maintenance role.

sections.heading: Sensor coverage
sections.text:
## Sensor coverage

The simulated database includes room temperature, humidity, supply-air temperature and cooling-unit power. There is no door-position sensor. Packaging hall readings are a separate access scope. The technician assigned to V-042 has access to Cooling room readings only.

documents.title: Danfoss Optyma Cooler
documents.preparation: Selected troubleshooting entries; symptom repeated for each row. Original wording retained.

sections.heading: 13 Troubleshooting / 2. Room temperature too high / 2.6
sections.text:
Symptom: Room temperature too high.

Possible cause 2.6: Excessive air infiltration due to open doors.

Possible corrective actions:
2.6.1 Check for doors seals and replace if necessary.
2.6.2 Keep doors closed as long as possible.

sections.heading: 13 Troubleshooting / 2. Room temperature too high / 2.7
sections.text:
Symptom: Room temperature too high.

Possible cause 2.7: Product has just been loaded into cold room.

Possible corrective action 2.7.1: Wait until product temperature is lower.

sections.heading: 13 Troubleshooting / 2. Room temperature too high / 2.4
sections.text:
Symptom: Room temperature too high.

Possible cause 2.4: Coil blocked with ice.

Possible corrective action 2.4.1: Make manual defrost in coil. Check defrost system.

documents.title: Danfoss AK-RC 305W-SD controller
documents.preparation: Selected prose from section 7; wiring diagrams and configuration tables excluded.

sections.heading: 7. Installation of the probes / Location of the ambient probe
sections.text: The probe should be located in a place that does not directly receive the flow of cold air from the evaporator. Preferably in its air aspiration area.

sections.heading: 7. Installation of the probes / Location of the evaporator probe
sections.text:
The probe must be located as near as possible to the inlet of refrigerant from the evaporator (close to the expansion valve) in the finned area. In certain evaporators, for example cubic ones, this inlet may be located on the front part of the battery, just behind the fan.

If defrost is done by electric heat, the probe must be located far away from them and, if possible, in the area of the evaporator where defrosting is slower, in other words, in the last area to defrost.

If the two conditions are not possible, the best possible compromise must be looked for.
